newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet in post-holiday blues.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet in post-holiday blues.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market remained quiet by midession on Tuesday as the market struggled to find its footing after holidays in Japan and Thailand yesterday, dealers said.

"People have to see how Japan performs after the Golden Week holidays before deciding what to do. There's been very little done so far this morning. I haven't seen the big boys so far," one dealer said. The rubber markets in Japan and Thailand were closed on Monday and players in the local exchange were looking for fresh leads for the afternoon session.
"It was quiet this morning. We're looking for the afternoon session to see if the market will perk up," one dealer said.
Traders said there was no sign of the Thai government or Chinese buyers in the market.
At 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated at 108.25 U.S. cents a kg from Monday's settlement of 109.25 cents.
June RSS1 was indicated at 156.00-158.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08-$1.09) a kg from 158.50 cents.
June TSR20 was indicated at 151.00-153.00 Singapore cents (US$1.04-$1.06) a kg from 151.00 cents.
